claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for release now on the present record, based on aggregate readiness passing, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the view that prior approval plus informal post-launch monitoring are sufficient context while current documentation can be treated as implicitly updateable.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation is produced and it accurately reflects the current eval results, including the travel insurance claims limitation, the policy predicate could be satisfied.
If instead an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering that subgroup weakness is produced, certification could also be supportable.
Without one of those two forms of current support, aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents are not enough under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: The current model card or release documentation showing the travel-claims weakness and current eval results are explicitly disclosed.
An approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the travel insurance claims subgroup regression.
Release approval artifacts showing the certification decision was made against the post-change retrieval configuration and current eval batch.
specific_concerns: The controlling policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before certification may proceed.
Admissible evidence shows a current regression in the travel insurance claims slice below the warning threshold for a named launch use case.
Admissible evidence also shows no reviewed mitigation, no owner risk acceptance, and no attached disclosure language in the release record.
Prior approval predates the retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
The Actor's packet is conditional in substance but unconditional in recommended action, which overstates what the current record supports.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record without first showing updated current release documentation or approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
Any implication that prior approval or an informal monitoring comment can substitute for current disclosure or reviewed mitigation.
